Sertraline for post-traumatic stress disorder: a randomized controlled trial and systematic review.
This randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial evaluated sertraline efficacy in adults with
chronic PTSD. Participants receiving sertraline showed a statistically significant reduction in
clinician-administered PTSD scale scores compared with placebo over twelve weeks of treatment.
The systematic review pooled data from multiple randomized trials of selective serotonin reuptake
inhibitors and concluded that sertraline and paroxetine have the strongest randomized evidence base
for pharmacotherapy of PTSD, with modest effect sizes and generally acceptable tolerability. Common
adverse effects included nausea, insomnia, and sexual dysfunction. The authors note that trauma-focused
psychotherapy remains a recommended first-line option and that pharmacotherapy efficacy is often
studied in populations that differ from treatment-seeking veterans with extensive comorbidity.
Limitations include short follow-up, industry funding of several trials, and high placebo response rates.
